title: Beatrix and the Static
premise: Petra Oyelaran is the last caretaker of Meridian, a terraforming project abandoned by an Earth that declared the colony legally dead while its people still lived. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, she discovers the signal originates from her own colony's sealed archive — a message recorded by the founders, proving Earth's government knowingly abandoned a viable settlement to cover up a terraforming scandal. Pursued by a corporate enforcer who needs the message destroyed before a peace summit between Earth and the breakaway colonies convenes, Petra must carry it across a dying world to a relay station. She delivers it at the summit's edge: the truth doesn't end the war cleanly, but it forces both sides to reckon with what was taken, and Petra plants the garden's first seeds in soil finally meant for the living.
about_author: Ansel Eastwick is a former hydrologist who spent six years on remote environmental monitoring stations before turning to fiction. He writes slow-burning science fiction about people who keep promises no one asked them to make.

chapters.title: The Gardener of Dead Air
chapters.summary: Petra tends Meridian's greenhouse alone, recording daily logs for settlers who will never arrive. Her POV establishes the colony's quiet decay and her stubborn ritual of care. Emotional beat: loneliness transmuted into devotion.

chapters.title: A Language No One Speaks
chapters.summary: Petra's radio picks up a structured signal in Old Terran Standard, extinct for two centuries. Tracing it, she finds it broadcasting from beneath Meridian's own sealed founder archive. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into unease — someone wanted this buried here.

chapters.title: What the Founders Sealed
chapters.summary: Petra breaches the archive and recovers a founder's testimony: Earth knew Meridian was viable when it cut funding, hiding a terraforming scandal. POV: Petra with interpolated archive recordings. Emotional beat: grief for the betrayed dead, and dawning purpose.

chapters.title: The Man from Reclamation
chapters.summary: Corporate auditor Davor Ilic arrives under pretext of asset recovery, but his questions reveal he knows what the archive holds. POV shifts to Ilic, showing his orders: destroy the message before the peace summit. Emotional beat: menace wearing a polite face.

chapters.title: Ash on the Glass
chapters.summary: Ilic burns the greenhouse as leverage; Petra escapes with the message core hidden in seed canisters. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: rage and loss — the garden she kept for the unborn, destroyed by the living.

chapters.title: The Long Gray Road
chapters.summary: Petra crosses the failed terraforming belt toward the coastal relay station, pursued by Ilic's drones. POV alternates Petra and Ilic, who begins doubting his employers' account. Emotional beat: endurance against a landscape that mirrors her despair.

chapters.title: Salt and Circuitry
chapters.summary: Petra shelters in a derelict fishing station and repairs an old maintenance android, Bex, whose fragmented memory holds fragments of the abandonment era. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: unexpected companionship; memory as inheritance.

chapters.title: Orders Are Orders
chapters.summary: Ilic's superiors escalate: authorize lethal force. He requests proof the colony was truly dead and receives a redacted file that answers nothing. POV: Ilic. Emotional beat: the first crack in his certainty.

chapters.title: The Summit Countdown
chapters.summary: News feeds reveal the Earth–Colonies peace summit convenes in eleven days at Meridian Station itself — the message must be delivered there or nowhere. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into urgency.

chapters.title: Bex Remembers
chapters.summary: Bex's recovered memory reveals the founders didn't all die — some were evacuated to the breakaway colonies, carrying half the testimony. The other half is in Petra's hands. POV: Bex. Emotional beat: the past insisting on being heard.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Shelf
chapters.summary: A superstorm traps Petra and Bex in a canyon; Ilic catches up but saves them from a collapse instead of taking the core. POV: rotating among all three. Emotional beat: enemies bound by shared survival.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Stranded together, Ilic interrogates Petra; she shows him the unredacted founder recording. He lets her go and reports the core destroyed. POV: Ilic. Emotional beat: justice chosen outside the law.

chapters.title: The Relay at Cape Verity
chapters.summary: Petra reaches the relay station and broadcasts the first half of the message openly; the colonies respond within hours — they have the matching half. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by fear of what comes next.

chapters.title: Reprisal
chapters.summary: Earth's fleet moves to jam the relay; Ilic is arrested for treason. Petra learns the summit delegation has landed at Meridian Station — and so has a second corporate kill team. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the cost of truth arriving due.

chapters.title: Return to the Garden
chapters.summary: Petra doubles back across hostile territory toward Meridian Station, carrying seed canisters and the message core through the burned ruins of her own work. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: returning to the wound as an act of hope.

chapters.title: The Kill Team
chapters.summary: The corporate team seizes the summit hall, holding delegates hostage until the broadcast is retracted. Petra infiltrates via the old greenhouse tunnels only she knows. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: terror mastered by intimate knowledge of home ground.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: In the seized hall, Petra plays the complete founder testimony — both halves joined — before delegates and cameras. The hostages are freed as soldiers refuse illegal orders. POV: ensemble. Emotional beat: the dead speaking, the living forced to listen.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Ilic testifies against his employers from custody; the scandal breaks open, but hardliners on both sides move to sabotage the ceasefire. POV: Ilic. Emotional beat: redemption without absolution.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Delegates vote on recognizing Meridian's dead and compensating the survivors' descendants; the war does not end, but a truce holds by a single decisive voice — a descendant of the evacuated founders. POV: Petra observing. Emotional beat: imperfect justice, still justice.

chapters.title: Seeds in Burned Ground
chapters.summary: Petra returns to the ruined greenhouse and plants the first seeds in scorched soil, joined by colonists and even a paroled Ilic. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed — gardening for the born at last.

chapters.title: The Signal Continues
chapters.summary: Petra resumes her logs, now addressed to listeners who answer. Bex archives every entry into the restored founder archive. POV: Petra. Emotional beat: memory transformed from burden into bridge.

chapters.title: Beatrix and the Static
chapters.summary: Years later, Petra's granddaughter Beatrix tends the thriving garden and finds Petra's final log: an instruction to keep listening, because static always carries something. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: closure as continuation — the message outlives the messenger.
